overall: On reconsideration, the AG found the Committee and Policy Subcommittee did not violate the Law, but the Equity Subcommittee violated it by creating minutes lacking substantive summaries of discussions, and ordered amended minutes.

allegations.summary: Policy Subcommittee minutes for 2020-2022 meetings were alleged to be insufficiently detailed and inaccurate.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons stated above, we find that the Committee and the Policy Subcommittee did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Equity Subcommittee minutes for 2020-2022 meetings were alleged to lack the detailed summaries of discussions required by law.
allegations.key_passage: we find that nearly all of the Equity Subcommittee’s minutes of meetings held between October 5, 2020, and June 21, 2022, include mentions that the Equity Subcommittee engaged in discussion without any summary of the discussion, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The Committee and Equity Subcommittee allegedly failed to obtain and document approval in minutes for school library book donations.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Committee and Equity Subcommittee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by failing to document approval for school library book donations in meeting minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant said minutes must show who started, presented or chaired the Equity Subcommittee meetings.
allegations.key_passage: there is no requirement in the Open Meeting Law that the minutes document who started, presented, or chaired a meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant raised many questions about matters (consultant engagement, a survey, prior-minutes approval) not shown to have been discussed at meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, in the absence of specific information indicating that the details or matters raised by the complainant were actually discussed, we do not review the sufficiency of the minutes with regard to such matters.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law by the Equity Subcommittee, with a note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.

Within 90 days, the Equity Subcommittee amends its minutes of meetings held between October 5, 2020, and June 21, 2022, to include summaries of the discussions on each topic, using any available means.
Within 90 days, the Equity Subcommittee certifies compliance to the Division; if it cannot create accurate amended minutes, it must explain in writing what efforts it made.
